speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC shows macrocytic anemia (MCV 100) which is unusual for a 1-month-old, and the normal echocardiogram rules out congenital heart disease as a cause for the apnea. Given the maternal rubella non-immunity and prematurity, I suspect Parvovirus B19 infection causing pure red cell aplasia. REQUEST TEST: Parvovirus B19 PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: Parvovirus B19 is ruled out, so the macrocytic anemia likely stems from nutritional deficiencies common in prematurity, such as folate or B12 deficiency. To narrow this down, does the infant have any neurological symptoms like irritability or developmental delay, and is the mother exclusively breastfeeding or using formula?

speaker: Doctor
text:
With B12 and folate levels normal, the macrocytic anemia and apnea in this premature infant strongly suggest iron deficiency anemia, which can present with macrocytosis in very young infants or be associated with other nutritional deficits. I will request an iron panel to confirm this suspicion.

REQUEST TEST: Iron Panel

speaker: Doctor
text:
Normal iron levels and B12/folate rule out common nutritional causes, so I must consider congenital bone marrow failure syndromes like Diamond-Blackfan Anemia, which presents with pure red cell aplasia and macrocytosis in infancy.

REQUEST TEST: Bone Marrow Biopsy
